messages:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: Pager triggered: PD alert PD-94821 -> svc-inference-prod-eu-west. Condition: p99_latency > 1200ms for 5m. Affects route: /v1/generate. Auto-page enabled.

pagerduty-bot: PagerDuty incident INC-94821 created and sent to current on-call. Escalation in 3m if not acknowledged.

Ava (oncall): ack INC-94821. I'm on it — starting triage. Quick ask: any recent rollouts to eu-west?

Raj: no code deploys in last 2 hours. Watching metrics now. Seeing p95 climb ~350ms -> 700ms, p99 jumping >1.2s. QPS steady.

Kai (eng-runtime): checking sidecar backlog and kv-cache hit rates. Sidecar queue depth increased from ~300 -> ~6k over 4m. KV cache eviction events spike at 03:12UTC. Suspect hot-key/backpressure + a burst of long-context requests.

Ava (oncall): can we confirm which model variants are hot? any large-batch requests?

Kai (eng-runtime): logs show many requests with seq_len ~4096 and batch_size ~256 hitting the large-gpu pool. Example log line: `req_id=abc123 lat=1350ms seq=4096 model=redwood-rlhf-large qsize=230`

Raj: also seeing autoscaler failing to add pods due to quota throttling in eu-west: `scale_request_rejected: quota_exceeded: gpu-pool-eu-west`. That explains queue growth.

Ava (oncall): ok two-pronged mitigation: (1) reduce incoming weight to large-gpu pool, route some traffic to smaller-quantized model; (2) free up capacity by dropping non-critical batchers and forcing immediate single-request dispatch for tail. I'll start routing change.

Kai (eng-runtime): I'm preparing the routing change. Command I'll apply:
```
# switch 20% traffic from large-gpu to small-quant-1
redwood route update --service inference --region eu-west --split "large-gpu=80,small-quant-1=20"
```

Ava (oncall): apply and post link to rollout.

Kai (eng-runtime): applied split at 03:20UTC. Watching. Metrics: queue depth trending down from 6k -> 2.5k over 90s. p99 falling slowly.

Maya (CS): got first customer report from ACME corp: slow responses on chat feature since ~03:10UTC. They see high tail latencies but mostly success. Any ETA for mitigation?

Ava (oncall): tell ACME we're aware and applying traffic reroute, expect partial improvement within 5-10m. I'll DM their CS lead and post a short update.

Raj: pushing another mitigation: temporarily increase allowed burst quota for autoscaler in eu-west to unblock rapid scale (need 10 extra GPUs). I'll request temporary quota bump via infra runbook.

Ava (oncall): go ahead, Raj. If quota path is slow, fallback plan: spin up a dedicated emergency pool in eu-west and attach pods there. Kai, can you prepare the `emergency-gpu` pool manifest?

Kai (eng-runtime): manifest ready. Command to create: `kubectl apply -f emergency-pool-eu-west.yaml -n prod` — will take ~60-90s to schedule if capacity free.

pagerduty-bot: Reminder: INC-94821 has 2m until auto-escalation.

Ava (oncall): I'm escalating to SRE lead to keep eyes on quota and customer comms. @Raj please confirm when quota request is filed.

Raj: filed quota request with infra (INC-94822) at 03:23UTC. Also started emergency pool creation as parallel path.

Kai (eng-runtime): emergency pool creation started at 03:24UTC. Pod scheduling log shows `Pending -> Running` for 12 new inference pods at 03:26UTC.

Ava (oncall): nice. Any observable latency change?

Kai (eng-runtime): p99 now down to ~890ms and decreasing. Queue depth down to ~900. Looks like routing + emergency pool helping.

Maya (CS): updated ACME: "We're seeing progressive improvements, routing changes have started to reduce tail latency. We're monitoring and will keep you posted." They replied :thumbsup:.

Raj: one more action: temporarily disable large batcher aggregation for /v1/generate for eu-west to avoid creating large long-running batches. Patch:
```
# disable batcher for route
redwood config set --route /v1/generate --region eu-west --batching enabled=false
```

Ava (oncall): applied. Note: this increases per-token cost but reduces queueing. Good trade for incident.

Kai (eng-runtime): confirming: batcher off, emergency pool healthy, routing split still 80/20. p95 ~280ms, p99 ~520ms. Trending stable.

pagerduty-bot: INC-94821 acknowledged by Ava. Auto-escalation cancelled.

Ava (oncall): marking customer-impact: "Degraded performance for a subset of users in eu-west". Severity: Sev2. Not seeing increased error rates, primarily latency.

Raj: I'll keep monitoring autoscaler / quota thread. Plan: leave routing split for 30m, then gradually move traffic back if stable. Also add a short-lived canary route to validate small-quant output quality.

Kai (eng-runtime): will run quality check on small-quant for representative prompt set. No regressions expected but will report.

Maya (CS): forwarding the incident summary to affected customers and offering a short status call if they want one.

Ava (oncall): handing off active monitoring to Raj for the next rotation. Summary for handoff: root cause suspected: simultaneous quota limit on autoscaler causing queue backlog + hot long-context requests triggering large-batch pressure. Mitigations: traffic split -> small-quant, emergency pool spun up, disabled batching for route, quota request filed. Current state: p99 down to ~520ms, queue <1k, no new customer error spikes.

Raj: accepting handoff. I'll watch for 30m and update on resolution or rollback. If p99 stays <600ms for 30m and no customer escalations, we'll start reverting routing and re-enable batching in controlled steps.

Ava (oncall): thanks team. Logging incident notes and will attach commands run + timeline to INC-94821.

Kai (eng-runtime): saved logs and will upload a brief post-incident note about autoscaler quota sensitivity and a suggested alert to warn before quota rejection persists.

Ava (oncall): closing the on-call thread. If anything changes, ping INC-94821.

pagerduty-bot: INC-94821 status: monitoring.

incident-bot: Incident thread summary saved to /incidents/INC-94821/summary.txt.

Raj: quick FYI for follow-up: add a kvcache warmup for small-quant when traffic shifts to reduce early miss storm. I'll file a follow-up ticket.

Maya (CS): ACME reported latency back to normal at 03:40UTC and appreciates the quick updates.

Ava (oncall): great. handing off complete.
